From 6a5b78b32d10cd7901f639870eca304b270769f9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Catalin Marinas <catalin.marinas@arm.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jun 2019 15:00:19 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: compat: No need for pre-ARMv7 barriers on an ARMv8
 system

Remove the deprecated (pre-ARMv7) compat barriers as they would not be used
on an ARMv8 system.

Fixes: a7f71a2c8903 ("arm64: compat: Add vDSO")
Signed-off-by: Catalin Marinas <catalin.marinas@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: Vincenzo Frascino <vincenzo.frascino@arm.com>

Cc: Ralf Baechle <ralf@linux-mips.org>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/include/asm/vdso/compat_barrier.h b/arch/arm64/include/asm/vdso/compat_barrier.h
index ea24ea856b07..fb60a88b5ed4 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/include/asm/vdso/compat_barrier.h
+++ b/arch/arm64/include/asm/vdso/compat_barrier.h
@@ -18,14 +18,7 @@
 #undef dmb
 #endif
 
-#if __LINUX_ARM_ARCH__ >= 7
 #define dmb(option) __asm__ __volatile__ ("dmb " #option : : : "memory")
-#elif __LINUX_ARM_ARCH__ == 6
-#define dmb(x) __asm__ __volatile__ ("mcr p15, 0, %0, c7, c10, 5" \
-				    : : "r" (0) : "memory")
-#else
-#define dmb(x) __asm__ __volatile__ ("" : : : "memory")
-#endif
 
 #if __LINUX_ARM_ARCH__ >= 8
 #define aarch32_smp_mb()	dmb(ish)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm64/include/asm/vdso/compat_barrier.h`**
   - The code block that defines memory barriers for different ARM architectures has been modified.
   - The conditional compilation checks for pre-ARMv7 architectures (specifically ARMv6 and below) have been removed.
   - The definition of `dmb` (data memory barrier) for ARMv6 and below has been eliminated, simplifying the code to only define `dmb` for ARMv7 and above.
   - The `#if __LINUX_ARM_ARCH__ >= 7` check remains, while the checks for ARMv6 and below have been removed entirely.

### Relationships

- The patch addresses the compatibility barriers in the ARM64 architecture by removing unnecessary definitions that are not applicable to ARMv8 systems. 
- This change is a cleanup that reflects the fact that ARMv8 systems do not require the pre-ARMv7 barriers, thus improving code maintainability and clarity.
- The modification is directly related to the previous commit identified in the patch, which added the vDSO (virtual Dynamically-linked Shared Object) support, indicating that the removal of these barriers is a follow-up fix to ensure that the code is optimized for ARMv8 without legacy support for older architectures.

This eliminates the potential for invoking unnecessary barriers, thus preventing synchronization issues and improving performance when running in compatibility mode.
